title.en: The Sight of My Father’s Back

edition.en: Text from Chinese Wikisource, transcribed from the essay collection The Sight of My Father’s Back (背影, 1928); first published in Literature Weekly (文學週報) no. 200, 22 November 1925.
edition.zh: 据维基文库，录自散文集《背影》（1928）；初刊于 1925 年 11 月 22 日《文学周报》第二百期。

basis.en: First published in 1925; the author died in 1948. Public domain by age: the author died before 1956 and the text was published before 1931.
basis.zh: 1925 年首次发表，作者卒于 1948 年。作者卒于 1956 年前、作品发表于 1931 年前，按年限属公有领域。

note.en: A heavy man in a black jacket climbs down onto the tracks and back up the far platform to buy his grown son some tangerines. Generations of Chinese schoolchildren have read this essay, and it earns that by restraint: it says almost nothing about love. Notice how often the son calls his younger self ‘too clever’, and how the whole piece is built on watching someone walk away.
note.zh: 一个穿黑布马褂的胖父亲，跳下铁道，又爬上对面的月台，去给已经成年的儿子买几个橘子。几代中国学生读过这篇散文，它配得上，靠的是克制：几乎一句也没有说到爱。留意儿子有多少次说当年的自己“太聪明”，以及整篇文章如何建立在看着一个人走远这件事上。

excerpt.orig: 等他的背影混入來來往往的人裏，再找不着了，我便進來坐下，我的眼淚又來了。
excerpt.en: When his back had mingled with the people coming and going and I could no longer find it, I went back in and sat down, and my tears came again.
excerpt.zh: 等他的背影混入来来往往的人里，再找不着了，我便进来坐下，我的眼泪又来了。

gloss.en: His father, Zhu Hongjun, had been head of the tobacco and wine tax office at Xuzhou; he lost the post in 1917, the winter of this story.
gloss.zh: 朱自清的父亲朱鸿钧原任徐州烟酒公卖局局长，1917 年卸职，就是文中的那年冬天。

gloss.en: 奔喪: to hurry home for the funeral of a close relative.
gloss.zh: 奔丧：从外地赶回料理长辈的丧事。

gloss.en: 典質: to pawn; things were pledged at a pawnshop for cash.
gloss.zh: 典质：把东西押给当铺换钱。

gloss.en: 賦閒: to be without a post. The phrase goes back to Pan Yue’s ‘Rhapsody on Living at Leisure’ (閒居賦), written after he left office.
gloss.zh: 赋闲：没有职业。语出晋代潘岳辞官后所作的《闲居赋》。

gloss.en: Pukou, on the north bank of the Yangzi opposite Nanjing, was the end of the railway to Tianjin; travellers crossed the river by ferry.
gloss.zh: 浦口：在南京对岸的长江北岸，是津浦铁路的南端终点，旅客须摆渡过江。

gloss.en: 茶房: an attendant at an inn or on a train or boat, who brought tea and ran errands.
gloss.zh: 茶房：旧时旅馆、车船上供应茶水、照料杂事的人。

gloss.en: 馬褂: a short jacket worn over the long gown, the respectable dress of the time.
gloss.zh: 马褂：穿在长袍外面的对襟短褂，当时是比较正式的穿着。

gloss.en: 大去: an old euphemism for dying. His father lived until 1945.
gloss.zh: 大去：婉指去世。他的父亲后来活到 1945 年。

note.en: A father’s heavy climb across the tracks for tangerines, told with a restraint that says almost nothing about love; a classic of modern Chinese prose, earned by its plainness.
note.zh: 父亲笨拙地爬过铁道去买橘子，写得克制，几乎不提一个爱字；现代散文的经典，靠的正是朴素。
